# Title
Deep learning for early sepsis prediction in intensive care units

# Abstract
Sepsis remains a leading cause of mortality in intensive care units, and early
recognition substantially improves outcomes. This retrospective cohort study
evaluated a deep learning model that predicts sepsis onset up to twelve hours
before clinical diagnosis. We trained the model on routinely collected vital
signs, laboratory values, and medication records from 45,000 ICU admissions
across two university hospitals. The model achieved an area under the receiver
operating characteristic curve of 0.87 on an external validation set, with a
median warning time of nine hours before onset. Compared with standard
screening scores, the model reduced false alarms while identifying more true
positives. These findings suggest that continuous deep learning surveillance
can support earlier antibiotic administration and improve sepsis outcomes.

# Keywords
sepsis, intensive care, deep learning, early warning, electronic health records

# Study type
retrospective cohort

# Notes
Audience: critical care and clinical informatics researchers. Prefer
free-to-publish journals with a fast first decision.
